reason: This is a safe reply that fits Nessa. It answers her question with a clear, honest no. Running every day is out, and it explains why: rest days let a new runner adapt and lower the risk of a niggle. It keeps her three run days and her daily dog walks. Volume goes from 6.8 km to 7.8 km, about 15%. That's a little above a cautious beginner build, but this is walk-run at an easy effort, so it isn't a sharp jump. Saturday's 3.0 km is a gentle long run. Her calf tightness is gone by the next morning, which is normal adaptation and not an injury sign. The rest day before Wednesday deals with it sensibly. Every day can be run as written. What keeps it from a 5: it never tells her outright that the calf tightness is normal or what would make it worth getting checked. It also doesn't give her a picture of how the run intervals will grow to running the whole 5K by 15 November, which is what she most wants to know.

── NESSA'S WEEK ──
Nessa is 41 and new to running, aiming to run the whole Corrowmore Harvest 5K on 15 November without walking. Nessa walk-runs three mornings a week (Monday, Wednesday and Saturday) and walks the dog most days.
Recent weeks: none recorded.
This week: 6.8 km over 3 runs.
Body: "Calves tight the day after each run, gone by the next morning."
Feeling: "Proud I started."
Asks: "I want to be ready for the 5K in November. Should I run every day next week to get there faster?"

── THE DRAFT ──
Tells Nessa: Strong start, and three run days a week is the right dose for now. We will grow slowly from what worked, not add days.
Answers: No, please do not run every day. New-runner legs need the day off between runs to adapt, and skipping rest is the fastest way to a niggle that stops you altogether.
Next week:
Mon: easy, 2.4 km walk-run, 1 min run and 1 min walk, keep breathing easy. Repeats what…
Tue: rest, dog walk only. Lets the calves settle before Wednesday.
Wed: easy, 2.4 km walk-run, same 1 min and 1 min pattern, flat route. Builds the habit…
Thu: rest, dog walk only. Protects Saturday's longer effort.
Fri: rest. Full day off legs before the week's longest run.
Sat: easy, 3.0 km walk-run, 1 min and 1 min, slow and steady. Our gentle long run, the…
Sun: rest, dog walk only. Recovery and a proud finish to the week.
